songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World

ai_show_review.summary: Stellar Cryptic>Drums>Other One suite, tight jams and vibrant acoustic set
ai_show_review.blurb: The concert starts with a relaxed acoustic first set that segues into a powerhouse second set dominated by the Cryptical Envelopment‑Drums‑The Other One sequence and big jam excursions. Jerry’s guitar shines on Casey Jones and New Speedway Boogie, while the drummers deliver a memorable Good Lovin’ drum jam.
ai_show_review.review:
On June 7, 1970 at Fillmore West the Dead delivered one of their most intriguingly balanced nights of the early ’70s. An intimate acoustic opening – featuring “Don’t Ease Me In,” “Friend Of The Devil,” and a plaintive “Cumberland Blues” – set a relaxed tone that gave way to a second‑set eruption. The highlight is undoubtedly the double‑Cryptical Envelopment sandwich with two drum interludes leading into an expansive “The Other One.” Reviewers rave about the seamless transition, the warbly yet warm tape character, and the intensity of Garcia’s lead work during the jam. The band kept the momentum rolling through a brisk “Sugar Magnolia,” classic “Casey Jones” (where Jerry’s guitar was called out as exceptional), and an exuberant “Good Lovin’” that featured a standout drum‑jam segment. Throughout, Phil laid down a solid bass foundation despite occasional vocal harmony slips on “Silver Threads And Golden Needles.” Bob kept the humor alive with banter and tight harmonies on “Me & My Uncle.” The night closes on a high note, making this show a must‑listen for fans of early‑70s Dead energy and improvisational daring.  

The three available recordings all capture the magic, but the Hollister soundboard (gd70-06-07.sbd.hollister.98.sbeok.shnf) offers the warmest acoustic fidelity while preserving the raw power of the “Cryptical>Drums>Other One” suite, making it the definitive listening choice.

best_recording.reason: Warm acoustic capture with a stellar Cryptical > Drums > Other One suite; good overall fidelity despite minor tape warble, making it the most balanced and complete version.

key_highlights: Cryptical Envelopment → Drums → The Other One suite is the show’s centerpiece
"New Speedway Boogie" showcases strong vocals and Garcia’s guitar work
"Casey Jones" features standout lead guitar and tight rhythm section
"Good Lovin'" includes an especially powerful drum jam

band_performance.Jerry: Vocals shine on New Speedway Boogie (with a hint of strain) and his guitar work is praised especially on Casey Jones; he also delivers intense, precise leads during the Other One sequence.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a solid bass foundation throughout; vocal harmonies are noted as off on Silver Threads And Golden Needles but otherwise supportive.
band_performance.Bob: Delivers strong harmony on Me & My Uncle and adds humorous stage banter about audience song requests.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are powerful, particularly in the quiet transition between Cryptical Envelopment and The Other One; also drives the memorable Good Lovin' drum jam.
band_performance.Billy: Locks in with Mickey for rhythmic power that lifts the crowd during the extended jams and the Good Lovin' segment.
